reason: The exposed line needs shelter, and wrapping it with reflective quilt stock seems like a useful way to protect the fittings and retain warmth.
expectation: I expect the quilt to wrap or insulate the well line, though I’m unsure how much protection it will give the fittings.

alternatives.reason: Bricks at the cabin perimeter could provide the local-material shelter, but I want to address the line directly first.

effect: The quilt insulates the hose while keeping its couplings accessible, and the result identifies a shallow trench as the next way to shelter the run.
reaction: I’m curious how the trench and perimeter shelter will work together.
reason: The shovel and insulated line match the suggested trench for sheltering the hose.
expectation: I expect to dig a shallow trench along the hose and place the insulated line in it, though the fittings may still need separate protection.

alternatives.reason: The bricks could shelter the cabin-side connections, but the exposed hose run has a clear next step.

effect: The insulated hose is now sheltered in a trench, with its connections accessible; its heat tracing still needs power. The remaining goal is to protect the cabin without putting weight on its skin.
reaction: The distinction between insulation slowing heat loss and powered heat tracing is useful.
reason: Placing the bricks at the cabin perimeter is the only available combination and fits the new goal.
expectation: I expect to build a freestanding brick barrier around part of the cabin, though I don't know exactly how it will protect it.

effect: The freestanding wall provides a separate support for packed material without loading the cabin’s pressure shell.
reaction: The separate footing makes the protection strategy clearer.
reason: The shovel and wall are the only available combination, and the result suggests packing local material against the wall.
expectation: I expect to shovel local material against the wall to add protection, though I’m unsure exactly what it will protect against.

effect: The berm shelters the service connections from drifting grit while keeping them accessible and leaving the window clear; the chapter’s goals are complete.
reaction: I like that the finished shelter accounts for both protection and access.

mostWorthwhile.text: Trenching the insulated line was most worthwhile because it showed how insulation slows heat loss while heat tracing still needs power.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the bricks and then shoveling against the wall felt somewhat predictable because each was the only available combination.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the hose trench to run away from the cabin perimeter or the wall to support packed material separately from the pressure shell.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the results made each construction step's purpose clear.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the settlement develops, especially because the construction choices have explained practical details along the way.
